sentences.text:
This appeal is filed by the injured- appellant/claimant seeking enhancement of compensation being aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 02.12.2009 passed in MVC No.342/2006 on the file of the Addl. Civil Judge (Sr.Dn.) & AMACT, Haveri (for short "the Tribunal").
2. Brief facts leading to filing of this appeal are that, on 31.08.2005 at about 1:15 p.m. on Huralikuppi- Mellagatti road, the driver of respondent No.1 drove the KSRTC bus bearing registration No.KA-25/F-1543, rashly and negligently, the claimant was travelling in the bus and said bus turtled towards the left side and caused accident.
Due to the accident, the claimant sustained grievous injuries.
He took treatment for a period of 21 days as an inpatient and spent huge amount.
He filed a claim petition before the Tribunal for the accidental injuries suffered by him in the road traffic accident, which occurred on 31.08.2005.
The respondent Nos.1 & 2 entered appearance before the Tribunal and opposed the claim petition by filing objections.
They denied the age, income and avocation of the injured.
It is denied that, the accident was caused due to the negligence of the driver of the KSRTC Bus.
They have sought for dismissal of the claim petition.
4. The Tribunal recorded the evidence of the parties.
The injured examined himself as PW1 and also examined the Doctor namely Dr.Kantesh Bheemakkanavar as PW2 and got marked the documents at Exs.P1 to P22.
The respondents got examined RW1 and no documents got marked.

The Tribunal considering the pleading and evidence on record, awarded total compensation in a sum of Rs.71,006/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of realisation.
Being aggrieved, the injured is in this appeal, seeking higher compensation.

Learned counsel Shri Harish S.Maigur appearing for the appellant submits that the Tribunal committed error in assessing the income of the injured, assessing the disability and has awarded meagre compensation on all other heads
Hence he seeks for reassessment of the compensation by allowing this appeal.

6. Per contra, Sri. S.C. Bhuti learned counsel appearing for the respondent No.1 supports the impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal and submits that the award passed by the Tribunal is just and proper, does not call for any modification.
Hence, he seeks to dismiss the appeal.

sentences.text: Heard the learned counsel appearing for the parties and perused the grounds of appeal and records of the Tribunal, the point that would arise for our consideration in this appeal is as to whether the impugned judgment and award of the tribunal calls for any interference?
The parties to the proceedings do not dispute the accident which occurred on 31.08.2005 and also the appellant sustaining fracture of forearm.

In support of his claim, the injured examined himself as PW1 and deposed with regard to his income, avocation and the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle and also examined the Doctor as PW2.

However, the tribunal has committed an error in considering his disability at 8%, which in my considered view, is contrary to the oral evidence of PW2, the Doctor and other medical records available before the Court.

The learned counsel for respondents also does not seriously dispute with regard to consideration of disability hence, this Court is of the considered view that it would be just and appropriate to reassess the disability of the appellant to the extent of 9% instead of 8% assessed by the Tribunal for the purpose of determination of compensation.

9. The pleading and evidence on record indicate that appellant was doing fabrication work and due to the NC: 2024:KHC-D:11428 said accidental injuries, he became disabled to carry out the same avocation, hence I am of the view that the entire compensation amount is required to be re-determined and accordingly I reassess the compensation taking note of the oral and documentary evidence on record.
10.
The Tribunal has assessed the income of the injured at Rs.3,000/- p.m.
admittedly the appellant has not placed on record any cogent and legally acceptable evidence with regard to the income.
Hence, I reassess the income of the injured notionally at Rs.3,500/- p.m. placing reliance on the Notional Income Chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
Further, the Tribunal has applied the appropriate multiplier of 18 based on the age of the injured at the time of accident.

Thus, the injured would be entitled to compensation under the head "loss of future income due to disability" at Rs.68,040/- (Rs.3,500/- x 12 x 18 x 9%).
NC: 2024:KHC-D:11428 11.

Taking note of the treatment provided to the injured-appellant/claimant, I reassess the compensation awarded under the head "Pain & Suffering" at Rs.30,000/- as against Rs.10,000/-
awarded by the Tribunal.
The Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.2,100/- towards "Nourishment food, attendant charges", which is on the lower side, hence, I reassess the same to Rs.18,000/-.
Further, the compensation of Rs.4,966/- awarded by the Tribunal towards "medical expenses" is retained as it is.

12. Further, the appellant has sustained the aforesaid injuries and fractures and was admitted as an inpatient in the Hospital for a substantial period, hence, I am of the considered view that the injured- appellant/claimant requires at least three month period to recover, so it would be just and proper to award Rs.10,500/- (Rs.3,500/- x 3 months) under the head "loss of income during the Manjunath Ramappa Ayyannanavar vs Managing Director Nwkrtc on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7732838/
3 period of treatment".

sentences.text: Considering the NC: 2024:KHC-D:11428 nature of injuries suffered by the claimant

, this Court award a sum of Rs.30,000/- towards "loss of amenities".
13.

Thus, the injured-appellant/claimant would be entitled to modified compensation on the following heads:
 Particulars Amount  (in Rs.)
 Pain & Suffering Rs.30,000/-
 Medical expenses Rs.4,966/-
 Nourishment, food and attendant Rs.18,000/-
 charges  Loss of income during the period of Rs.10,500/-
 treatment  Loss of future income due to Rs.68,040 /-
 disability  Loss of amenities Rs.30,000/-

Total Rs.1,61,506/-
14. Thus, the injured-appellant/claimant would be entitled to total compensation of Rs.1,61,506/- as against Rs.71,006/- awarded by the Tribunal.

15. In the result, the following:
ORDER (i) The appeal stands allowed in part.

NC: 2024:KHC-D:11428 (ii) The impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal is modified to an extent that the injured-appellant/claimant would be entitled to total compensation of Rs.1,61,506/- as against Rs.71,006/-awarded by the Tribunal.
(iii) The enhanced compensation amount shall carry interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of payment.

(iv) The respondent - Corporation to pay the entire compensation amount along with interest to the injured-appellant/claimant within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
(v) The injured-appellant/claimant is not entitled to any interest for the delayed period of 2316 says in preferring the appeal as per the order dated 17.01.2020.
(vi) Apportionment, deposit and disbursement shall be made as per the award of the Tribunal.
